column1: # producer   by hand: Essenthos's versification rules, read by forge frame
# The numbering schemes the versification data (TVTMS) names, and the tradition each belongs to.
# The first scheme of a tradition is the one the tradition is named after; the rest are its variants.
# The order is the order they are weighed in: where two schemes of a tradition answer an edition's
# tests equally, the earlier one is taken. The data names twelve Greek schemes, not one, and which of
# them an edition follows is answered by the edition rather than by its language. The Russian schemes
# are absent from the data, so a Synodal text cannot be placed from this source and has to say so
# rather than fall back to its own numbering and look right.
#   tradition  original, english, septuagint or vulgate
#   scheme     the scheme's name as the data writes it in its SourceType column
#   divided    for an undivided scheme, the divided scheme it is written against; '-' for the others.
#              The data writes an undivided scheme as only the rows that differ from the divided one
#              (in Exodus 40 three rows about 38:27 and nothing about the renumbering of the chapter),
#              so it is read as the divided scheme's rows with its own in place of the ones about the
#   why        what the row says beyond its name, or '-' where its name is all the data says of it
